reading_flow.context_title: Table 6.6: Some common naturally occurring fatty acids
reading_flow.text: Table 6.6 lists common naturally occurring fatty acids categorized into saturated and unsaturated types, detailing their number of carbons, common name, chemical structure or formula, and melting point in degrees Celsius. Saturated fatty acids include: Lauric acid with 12 carbons, formula CH3(CH2)10COOH, melting point 44 degrees Celsius; Myristic acid with 14 carbons, formula CH3(CH2)12COOH, melting point 58 degrees Celsius; Palmitic acid with 16 carbons, formula CH3(CH2)14COOH, melting point 63 degrees Celsius; Stearic acid with 18 carbons, formula CH3(CH2)16COOH, melting point 69 degrees Celsius; and Arachidic acid with 20 carbons, formula CH3(CH2)18COOH, melting point 77 degrees Celsius. Unsaturated fatty acids include: Palmitoleic acid with 16 carbons, formula CH3(CH2)5 CH equals CH(CH2)7COOH, melting point 0 degrees Celsius; Oleic acid with 18 carbons, formula CH3(CH2)7 CH equals CH(CH2)7COOH, melting point 13 degrees Celsius; Linoleic acid with 18 carbons, formula CH3(CH2)4 CH equals CH CH2 CH equals CH(CH2)7COOH, melting point negative 5 degrees Celsius; and Linolenic acid with 18 carbons, formula CH3 CH2 CH equals CH CH2 CH equals CH CH2 CH equals CH(CH2)7COOH, melting point negative 11 degrees Celsius.

reading_flow.text: The physical properties of a fatty acid depend on the length of the hydrocarbon chain and the degree of unsaturation. The melting points of saturated fatty acids increase with increasing molecular weight because of increased van der Waals interactions between the molecules.
